title: An Optimizing Framework on MLIR for Efficient FPGA-based Accelerator Generation
problem: FPGA programming is non-trivial and existing HLS tools have limited scope and capability to support sufficient FPGA-oriented transformations and optimizations. Traditional approaches rely on single-level intermediate representations that introduce excessive information and make debugging difficult.
motivation: Customized accelerators like FPGAs are essential for meeting increasing computing demands while respecting constrained resource and power budgets.
method: POM uses a multi-level MLIR framework with three abstraction layers to perform optimizations at appropriate IR levels. It integrates the polyhedral model into MLIR to enable advanced dependence analysis and FPGA-oriented loop transformations through polyhedral manipulations. A domain-specific language (DSL) with scheduling primitives enables concise computation specification, while an automatic design space exploration engine searches for high-performance optimization schemes.
key_novelty: Integration of polyhedral model into multi-level MLIR to enable systematic and flexible FPGA-oriented loop transformations and optimizations at appropriate abstraction levels.
contributions: Three-layer IR abstraction providing better flexibility, extensibility, and systematicness compared to single-level IR approaches
Integration of polyhedral model with MLIR for advanced dependence analysis and convenient loop transformation capabilities
User-friendly DSL with rich scheduling primitives for concise accelerator specification
Automatic design space exploration engine for efficient optimization scheme discovery and accelerator generation

metrics.speedup: 6.46× average on benchmark suites, 6.06× average on real-world applications

primary_theme: Multi-level IR framework for FPGA compiler optimization
